requirement: A response closed before the Content-Length number of octets is incomplete and the recipient closes its connection
notes: Orderly peer half-close supplies EOF. A Deferred holds the client resource alive until its own transport closure is observed; fixture cleanup cannot satisfy closure.

requirement: A request closed before the Content-Length number of octets is incomplete and the recipient closes its connection
notes: EchoBody observes only fully consumed bodies. A completed warm-up exchange precedes the malformed upload; every incomplete upload ends with explicit half-close. Optional error status lines preserve permitted obs-text reason bytes and reject control octets (RFC 9112 Section 4). A Connection: close warmup reports a typed observation limit before the incomplete stimulus; it cannot establish coverage.

requirement: If a recipient times out before Content-Length octets arrive it treats the message as incomplete and closes
notes: The frozen target does not expose an application timeout trigger or a configurable short receive deadline. The test deadline is inconclusive and cannot substitute for a protocol timeout.

requirement: A request-body receive timeout before Content-Length octets arrive marks the request incomplete and closes
notes: The frozen target does not expose request-body timeout configuration. Intentionally leaving EchoBody uploads unfinished would also risk fixture-release hangs; no absence interval is treated as rejection.

requirement: A valid Content-Length delimits exactly that many octets independently of a subsequent orderly close
notes: Positive controls distinguish complete length-delimited messages from truncated ones.

requirement: A request with neither Transfer-Encoding nor Content-Length has zero body length rather than a close-delimited body
notes: This boundary observes a complete bodyless request followed by client half-close; malformed extra octets are covered by the separate framing inventory.

requirement: A response without declared framing consumes the octets preceding orderly connection closure
notes: Covers binary and empty HTTP/1.1 bodies and the HTTP/1.0 compatibility case; the scripted peer explicitly sends EOF.

requirement: A response with Transfer-Encoding whose final coding is not chunked is delimited by connection closure
notes: No non-chunked transfer-coding EOF case is authored in this lifecycle fragment; capability and decoding alternatives need coordination with the framing inventory. Ordinary no-framing EOF cases do not cover this branch.

requirement: A server generates encoding- or length-delimited responses whenever possible instead of relying on closure
notes: The server cases parse returned bodies but do not independently assert this recommendation across all Reply and ReplyChunks scenarios; a closure-delimited successful response can be legitimate.

requirement: The chunked-body grammar requires the trailer section and its final CRLF after the last chunk
notes: Both body consumption and the response trailers effect are forced before accepting successful completion.

requirement: The uploaded chunked-body grammar requires the trailer section and its final CRLF after the last chunk
notes: A last chunk by itself cannot make EchoBody publish a completed request when the trailer section is truncated. A Connection: close warmup reports a typed observation limit before the incomplete stimulus; it cannot establish coverage.

requirement: A server may send an error response before closing an incomplete request; silent closure is permitted
notes: Accepts actual EOF/reset with no response or an error status after optional informational heads. Bytes preceding reset are retained. Timeout and unrelated exceptions never prove rejection. The finite 64 KiB response observation and 16 informational-head ceiling report WireObservationLimit, not a protocol violation or successful rejection. A Connection: close warmup reports a typed observation limit before the incomplete stimulus; it cannot establish coverage.

requirement: A client records a response truncated within the status line as incomplete
notes: The raw peer finishes the request read before sending the truncated status line; only the target response operation is attempted.

requirement: A client records a response truncated within a header field as incomplete
notes: No terminating field CRLF or header-section empty line is sent.

requirement: A client cannot treat a response whose header section lacks its terminating empty line as complete
notes: The Content-Length field itself is intact; the response head terminator alone is missing.

requirement: Incomplete-response cache requirements are delegated to RFC 9111 section 3.3
notes: Caching is explicitly outside the baseline scope; no cache adapter is present.

requirement: A status whose meaning depends on missing fields can require a repeated request to decide what action to take
notes: The wire cases reject partial heads. Status-specific application decisions and policy for repeating requests are excluded general semantics.

requirement: A chunked message ending within its chunk-size line is incomplete
notes: A deterministic peer half-close supplies the truncation; no wall-clock silence is interpreted as completion or rejection.

requirement: A chunked message ending before all chunk-data octets arrive is incomplete
notes: A deterministic peer half-close supplies the truncation; no wall-clock silence is interpreted as completion or rejection.

requirement: A chunked message ending within the chunk-data CRLF is incomplete
notes: A deterministic peer half-close supplies the truncation; no wall-clock silence is interpreted as completion or rejection.

requirement: A chunked message without its zero-sized last chunk is incomplete
notes: A deterministic peer half-close supplies the truncation; no wall-clock silence is interpreted as completion or rejection.

requirement: A chunked message ending within its chunk-size line is incomplete
notes: A deterministic peer half-close supplies the truncation; no wall-clock silence is interpreted as completion or rejection. A Connection: close warmup reports a typed observation limit before the incomplete stimulus; it cannot establish coverage.

requirement: A chunked message ending before all chunk-data octets arrive is incomplete
notes: A deterministic peer half-close supplies the truncation; no wall-clock silence is interpreted as completion or rejection. A Connection: close warmup reports a typed observation limit before the incomplete stimulus; it cannot establish coverage.

requirement: A chunked message ending within the chunk-data CRLF is incomplete
notes: A deterministic peer half-close supplies the truncation; no wall-clock silence is interpreted as completion or rejection. A Connection: close warmup reports a typed observation limit before the incomplete stimulus; it cannot establish coverage.

requirement: A chunked message without its zero-sized last chunk is incomplete
notes: A deterministic peer half-close supplies the truncation; no wall-clock silence is interpreted as completion or rejection. A Connection: close warmup reports a typed observation limit before the incomplete stimulus; it cannot establish coverage.

requirement: A body with fewer received octets than a valid Content-Length is incomplete
notes: Separate cases cover an entirely absent body and a nonempty proper prefix on both recipient roles.

requirement: An otherwise complete length- or chunk-delimited response stays complete at orderly EOF
notes: The negative truncated-message cases do not establish acceptance of complete messages; these positive controls do.

requirement: A response without chunked coding or Content-Length is complete at orderly close if its entire header section arrived
notes: Binary octets are compared exactly; transport EOF is sent after the complete header section.

requirement: An underlying transport error prevents an otherwise close-delimited response from being considered complete
notes: RawPeer exposes orderly half-close but no portable deliberate TCP reset/error injection. TLS incomplete closure is separately excluded; an arbitrary fixture exception is not evidence of this behavior.

requirement: Client configuration and the target URI determine transport and routing as described by RFC 9110 section 7.3
notes: The baseline fixes plaintext loopback TCP and explicit endpoint addresses; proxy routing and other transport mappings are excluded.

requirement: Each HTTP connection maps to one transport connection; establishment details are outside RFC 9112
notes: Socket establishment and transport protocol selection are fixture mechanics, not an additional HTTP wire requirement.

requirement: Response order corresponds to the order of requests on the same connection
notes: Distinct echoed bodies identify response order rather than merely counting responses. RFC 9112 Section 6.3 permits 411 for a request without Content-Length; that branch does not establish chunk decoding, body drainage, or pipeline/reuse coverage. Loss of persistence after a verified first response reports an unavailable coverage prerequisite, never mandatory-order failure or ordering success (RFC 9112 9.3.1/9.6).

requirement: An API-visible informational response is bodyless; a visible final response has its declared content
notes: A 100 and 103 precede a distinct 200 body. The API may expose a bodyless interim response. Final-response continuation is unobservable in that branch; actual subsequent-request association is covered separately by h1.client.interaction-interim-next-request-association.

requirement: A client with multiple outstanding requests maintains send order and associates a response with the first request lacking a final response
notes: ClientDriver has no operation requiring multiple outstanding requests on the same HTTP/1 connection. Concurrent exchanges may use separate connections or serialize; no test may invent a mandatory client pipelining feature.

requirement: Data arriving without an outstanding request must not be considered a valid response
notes: The frozen single-accepted-socket fixture cannot complete a subsequent valid exchange if the target correctly closes and reconnects. A bounded reconnection-aware fixture and a no-outstanding-request barrier are needed.

requirement: A client should close when unsolicited non-CRLF data makes message delimitation ambiguous
notes: Requires the same deterministic idle-client observation and reconnect support as the unsolicited-response validity gap.

requirement: One or more unsolicited CRLF octet pairs may be discarded rather than requiring closure
notes: Needs a conditional reuse-or-reconnect oracle; closure itself is also permitted, so requiring reuse would incorrectly reject a valid implementation.

requirement: HTTP implementations should support persistent HTTP/1.1 connections
notes: Explicitly a recommendation; a second request is issued only after the first response completes.

requirement: HTTP clients should support successive exchanges on persistent HTTP/1.1 connections
notes: These recommendation cases require reuse of the accepted connection; timeout remains inconclusive rather than proving a mandatory-protocol violation.

requirement: A close connection option takes precedence over all persistence defaults or keep-alive options
notes: Covers an HTTP/1.1 option list in both recipient roles and the HTTP/1.0 server branch.

requirement: An HTTP/1.1 message without close permits connection persistence without an explicit keep-alive option
notes: The first request and scripted response omit Connection; distinct second bodies exercise message boundaries.

requirement: An eligible non-proxy recipient may honor HTTP/1.0 keep-alive when that option is present
notes: Optional honor-or-close behavior is not exercised. Http1Wire.Response does not expose the response version, limiting a precise version-dependent reuse oracle; the no-keep-alive branch is covered separately.

requirement: An HTTP/1.0 request without keep-alive does not persist after its response
notes: Requires the complete response before observing transport closure.

requirement: A client must not continue using a connection after an HTTP/1.0 response without keep-alive
notes: The positive HTTP/1.0 EOF case proves body completion only. No-reuse across a subsequent exchange requires a reconnection-aware fixture, which the frozen CaseContext.client does not provide.

requirement: A client that does not support persistence sends close on every request
notes: No frozen target configuration disables persistent support. Supplying Connection: close on one application request does not prove automatic marking of all requests by a nonpersistent client.

requirement: A server without persistence sends close on every non-informational response
notes: No frozen target configuration disables persistent support; the obligation is conditional and cannot be inferred from a single explicitly configured close response.

requirement: A client may send further requests while the connection remains persistent and has not received close
notes: Exercises the permitted path but does not turn optional client pipelining into a requirement.

requirement: Messages on a reused connection have self-defined boundaries rather than depending on connection closure
notes: The first message completes and the next is independently decoded on the same open socket. RFC 9112 Section 6.3 permits 411 for a request without Content-Length; that branch does not establish chunk decoding, body drainage, or pipeline/reuse coverage. Loss of persistence after a verified first response reports an unavailable coverage prerequisite, never mandatory-order failure or ordering success (RFC 9112 9.3.1/9.6).

requirement: A server that ignores a fixed-length request body drains its entire body or closes after the response
notes: The body contains a complete request-shaped byte sequence. Either actual closure or only the following real request is permitted; the body must never become an application request. EOF during a partial second response head establishes closure only, not a valid second response; other malformed-wire errors remain failures.

requirement: A server that ignores a chunked request body drains through chunk/trailer termination or closes
notes: Includes a trailer and a following request. Actual EOF/reset is accepted only after the first valid request/response, never around setup. RFC 9112 Section 6.3 permits 411 for a request without Content-Length; that branch does not establish chunk decoding, body drainage, or pipeline/reuse coverage. EOF during a partial second response head establishes closure only, not a valid second response; other malformed-wire errors remain failures. The 411 branch observes closure or a valid second response followed by closure and checks all currently published application paths for body misdispatch; partial post-411 response syntax and asynchronous future publication remain observation limits.

requirement: A client reusing a connection consumes the complete prior response message
notes: The application explicitly consumes the body and releases its response resource before the next exchange; the chunked variant includes a trailer.

requirement: A client abandoning a partially consumed response must read the remainder if it reuses that connection
notes: The complete-consumption cases do not cover cancellation or early body release. A fixture supporting conditional old-socket drain versus a replacement connection is needed.

requirement: A proxy must not maintain persistence with an HTTP/1.0 client
notes: Proxy forwarding is excluded; the server target is an origin endpoint, not an intermediary.

requirement: Appendix C.2.2 explains legacy HTTP/1.0 Keep-Alive and Proxy-Connection compatibility issues
notes: The current persistence branches are inventoried above. Historical proxy workarounds and optional legacy mechanisms are not independent required origin behavior.

requirement: Connection management anticipates asynchronous close events and recovers where appropriate
notes: No portable abrupt-close injection or reconnecting raw-listener fixture is exposed by CaseContext.client. EOF message-completeness tests do not prove retry recovery.

requirement: RFC 9110 section 9.2.2 defines conditions for automatically retrying outstanding requests
notes: General method semantics and automatic retry policy are excluded; the wire-ordering restriction on retried pipelines remains an explicit gap below.

requirement: A client supporting persistence may pipeline requests before receiving corresponding responses
notes: The frozen client driver does not promise pipelining, and the RFC does not require it. No test requires this optional feature merely to achieve coverage.

requirement: A server may process a pipeline in parallel when every method is safe
notes: Parallel application scheduling and the general safe-method classification are outside the target contract; serialized processing remains valid and response order is tested independently.

requirement: A server sends pipelined responses in the order their requests arrived
notes: Both requests are available before any response is read; distinct bodies make reordering observable. RFC 9112 Section 6.3 permits 411 for a request without Content-Length; that branch does not establish chunk decoding, body drainage, or pipeline/reuse coverage. Loss of persistence after a verified first response reports an unavailable coverage prerequisite, never mandatory-order failure or ordering success (RFC 9112 9.3.1/9.6).

requirement: A client that pipelines retries unanswered requests when closure prevents receipt of their responses
notes: Client pipelining and reconnection cannot be required through the frozen fixture; no retry is inferred from a timeout.

requirement: When retrying a failed pipeline a client must not pipeline immediately after connection establishment
notes: Needs a target capable of client pipelining and a raw peer that accepts the replacement connection and observes the retry before responding.

requirement: A user agent avoids pipelining after a non-idempotent method until the final status unless it can recover partial failures
notes: General method semantics and retry policy are outside baseline scope; no assertion assumes that POST replay is categorically forbidden.

requirement: An intermediary may pipeline forwarded requests and retry unanswered idempotent sequences
notes: Proxy forwarding and intermediary retry policy are explicitly excluded.

requirement: An intermediary with unsafe unanswered requests forwards received responses and closes outbound connections
notes: No intermediary topology exists in the frozen target contract; origin wire cases do not cover this rule.

requirement: Clients ought to limit simultaneous server connections but no numerical maximum is mandated
notes: Connection-pool sizing and denial-of-service policy are not falsifiable as a fixed wire limit; the TCK does not invent a maximum.

requirement: Persistent connections impose no requirement on the existence or duration of idle timeouts
notes: No arbitrary silence interval is turned into proof that a target violated persistence or rejected a message.

requirement: A client or server choosing to time out should issue graceful transport closure
notes: The target contract lacks controllable protocol timeout settings; test deadlines cannot stand in for target timeout behavior.

requirement: Implementations monitor open connections for peer closure and promptly reclaim connection resources
notes: EOF is observed in individual exchanges, but no target resource-count or idle-connection closure oracle is exposed. Completion during fixture shutdown is not independent proof.

requirement: A server may close a transport connection instead of continuing a persistent exchange
notes: The drain-or-close assertions explicitly preserve closure as the allowed alternative; they do not require a next response after observed EOF/reset. RFC 9112 Section 6.3 permits 411 for a request without Content-Length; that branch does not establish chunk decoding, body drainage, or pipeline/reuse coverage. The 411 branch observes closure or a valid second response followed by closure and checks all currently published application paths for body misdispatch; partial post-411 response syntax and asynchronous future publication remain observation limits.

requirement: Servers sustain persistent connections when possible and use transport flow control for temporary overload
notes: No deterministic overload or backpressure control exists for server application scheduling in the frozen scenario API. Basic persistence support is covered separately.

requirement: An uploading client monitors the connection for a response indicating the server refuses the body and is closing
notes: A fixed 32 KiB prefix followed by three Deferred-blocked octets has a matching Content-Length. The peer positively checks the complete exact prefix before returning 413 with close while the suffix remains blocked. This crosses ordinary write coalescing without requiring tiny-chunk flushing; a target buffering more can leave the stimulus unestablished. The eight-second deadline remains inconclusive, with the transcript distinguishing missing stimulus from a post-413 observation limit; no timeout is evidence of rejection.

requirement: A client receiving an error that closes the connection ceases sending the body and closes its side
notes: After exact receipt of the fixed 32 KiB prefix and the peer 413, the upload finalizer and actual client transport closure are observed while the client resource remains alive and the three-byte suffix remains blocked; the raw peer sends no EOF to manufacture closure. Larger buffering or a post-413 deadline remains an observation limit, not proof of violating this SHOULD recommendation.

requirement: A sender intending to close should advertise the close connection option
notes: Explicitly configured close cases establish receiver behavior; they do not expose every internal planned-close path or prove automatic advertisement.

requirement: The field name Close is reserved to avoid collision with the close connection option
notes: This is a registration/design constraint; rejection of an arbitrary Close header is not required and no such rejection is invented.

requirement: A client sending close closes after reading the corresponding final response
notes: The scripted final response omits Connection. A Deferred prevents client-resource release from satisfying the expected closure.

requirement: A client that sends close must not send another request on that connection
notes: The closure case observes no further wire bytes before EOF but does not issue another application exchange. Proving non-reuse after a subsequent exchange needs a reconnecting fixture.

requirement: A server receiving close initiates closure after its final response
notes: Requires a complete first response before observing EOF/reset; subsequent bytes produce a protocol failure.

requirement: A server should send close in its final response to a request carrying close
notes: Current cases require closure and prohibit a subsequent request but do not require the recommended response option; this is distinct from the mandatory close action.

requirement: A server receiving close must not process later requests on that connection
notes: A second complete request is already pipelined. Requires no second response bytes and no additional currently available application observation after closure; arbitrary later side effects are outside the wire observation contract.

requirement: A server sending close initiates transport closure after that response
notes: The application scenario supplies Connection: close; the first response body must be fully delivered before closure.

requirement: A server sending close must not process any further requests received on that connection
notes: The following request is written before the first response is read; no second response or queued observation is permitted after observed closure.

requirement: A client receiving close closes after reading the containing response
notes: Neither raw peer half-close nor client resource release can satisfy this check; the transport close must occur while both are held open.

requirement: A client receiving close ceases sending new requests on that connection
notes: Closure is directly tested, but a later application exchange and replacement-connection selection are not available through the single accepted raw socket.

requirement: A client should not assume already-pipelined requests will be processed after close
notes: Requires observable client pipelining plus per-request completion outcomes; ClientDriver does not promise pipelining on one connection.

requirement: Staged write-side closure followed by reading helps avoid TCP reset loss of the final response
notes: The RFC describes a typical mitigation without requiring a particular TCP shutdown algorithm. Cases require the expected complete response before closure and do not mandate a specific FIN/reset sequence.

requirement: A client transport half-close neither determines request framing nor implies abandonment of the response
notes: These positive controls fully delimit the request before half-close and still require the matching complete response. RFC 9112 Section 6.3 permits 411 for a request without Content-Length; that branch does not establish chunk decoding, body drainage, or pipeline/reuse coverage.

requirement: TLS initiation and HTTPS identity/handshake requirements apply to secure transports
notes: TLS and ALPN are outside the plaintext baseline; no claims are made about secure connection establishment.

requirement: TLS endpoints follow closure-alert and incomplete-close processing rules
notes: TLS is outside the baseline. Orderly TCP EOF is deliberately distinguished from TLS incomplete-close rules.

requirement: Clients determine response completeness and recover gracefully from TLS incomplete close while servers tolerate it as specified
notes: No TLS adapter or closure-alert control is exposed; plaintext EOF cases must not be reported as TLS coverage.

requirement: message/http encloses one message subject to MIME line-length and encoding restrictions
notes: MIME encapsulation and application content formats are outside the wire-message baseline.

requirement: A consumer of message/http replaces obsolete line folding with one or more spaces
notes: This is the explicit encapsulated-message exception to ordinary HTTP field parsing; the testkit does not consume message/http payloads.

requirement: message/http version and msgtype parameters are optional and only 7bit 8bit or binary encodings are permitted
notes: Media-type parameter interpretation and MIME content-transfer encoding are excluded application semantics.

requirement: application/http encloses one or more request messages or response messages without mixing types
notes: An on-wire persistent connection is not application/http encapsulation; the media type is excluded.

requirement: application/http has optional version and msgtype parameters and binary encoding with appropriate email transfer encoding
notes: Media encapsulation and email transport are outside the protocol target contract.

requirement: Response splitting exploits ordered request-to-response association on persistent connections
notes: The response-order cases cover the ordering primitive, not malicious injected second responses. Cross-section smuggling/splitting stimuli are assigned to a separate audit fragment.

requirement: Preserving request body boundaries prevents body bytes being interpreted as a hidden extra request
notes: This is a narrow lifecycle boundary probe. Conflicting framing and cross-parser differential smuggling are independently inventoried elsewhere. RFC 9112 Section 6.3 permits 411 for a request without Content-Length; that branch does not establish chunk decoding, body drainage, or pipeline/reuse coverage. The 411 branch observes closure or a valid second response followed by closure and checks all currently published application paths for body misdispatch; partial post-411 response syntax and asynchronous future publication remain observation limits.

requirement: Length and chunk delimiters expose truncated messages despite the lack of a general HTTP integrity mechanism
notes: These cases detect incomplete messages only; they do not claim authentication or protection against arbitrary modification.

requirement: TLS and optional integrity extensions can protect message integrity beyond plaintext framing
notes: TLS, user-agent presentation, message signatures, and optional integrity extensions are excluded.

requirement: Connection consists of a list of token connection options
notes: Exercises comma-separated and multiple-field lists with a close option following keep-alive. The broader token grammar belongs to the syntax inventory.

requirement: Connection options are case-insensitive
notes: Mixed-case ClOsE must retain the normal close behavior in both recipient roles.

requirement: List parsing tolerates a reasonable number of empty Connection list elements as specified by RFC 9110 section 5.6.1
notes: No Connection-specific leading/trailing/adjacent-comma variants are currently present; list syntax coverage of other fields does not automatically cover this parser.

requirement: A sender of a connection control field lists that field name in Connection
notes: TE provides a core concrete instance, but these lifecycle cases do not exercise sender generation of TE and its matching Connection option. Optional control extensions are not enabled.

requirement: An intermediary parses Connection before forwarding the message
notes: Proxy forwarding is explicitly outside the baseline and no intermediary target exists.

requirement: An intermediary removes every header or trailer named by each connection option and removes or replaces Connection itself
notes: Origin/client fixtures cannot demonstrate intermediary removal or forwarding of hop-by-hop fields.

requirement: An intermediary removes or replaces known hop-by-hop fields even when not named by Connection
notes: The Proxy-Connection Keep-Alive TE Transfer-Encoding and Upgrade forwarding cases require an intermediary topology, which is excluded.

requirement: A sender must not list a field intended for all recipients as a connection option
notes: No generated-request or generated-response case currently checks prohibited end-to-end field names such as Cache-Control in Connection. Receiver rejection is not required by this sender prohibition.

requirement: A parameterless connection option need not have a corresponding field present in the message
notes: Connection: close is exercised without a Close field; requiring a matching field would break the complete response and close assertions.

requirement: A connection-specific field received without its matching option usually indicates improper forwarding and ought to be ignored
notes: No optional control-field extension is enabled, and ignoring a field is not a universal mandatory rejection rule. The TE sender rule is a separate explicit gap.

requirement: Authors of a new parameterless connection option reserve the corresponding field name
notes: This is a specification-author and registry constraint, not executable endpoint behavior.
